## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷakuṇālajātaka* (Ja 464), titled *The Shorter Tale of the Cuckoo* in modern translation, is a narrative text preserved in the canonical Pali Jātaka collection. Its opening lemma begins with the phrase "Small of wit", and the traditional commentary notes that the full account of this birth story is given under the *Kuṇālajātaka*. In epigraphic and temple records from the Pagan period in Burma, the title appears in diverse orthographic and lexical variants, including *Cūlakuņāla* (at Hpetleik, Gubyaukgyi [Wetkyi-in], and Shwezigon), *Cūlakunāla* (at Ananda), *Cūlakuņālā* (at Ajagona), as well as *Cūlasakuna* (Thingaraza), *Cūvasakuna* (Gubyaukgyi [Myinkaba]), and *Cūlawaw* (Winido) [Win Than Tun 2002].

 Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms this close internal relationship, showing 9 matching segments spanning §1.1–12.4 of Ja 464 aligned with identical text in Ja 536 (§63.4–75.4), in addition to 9 matches shared with the fifth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (§1.2–12.4 ↔ §4321–4355) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-language machine alignments with Tibetan texts in the Tengyur, including the *Jinamārgāvatāra* (D3964) and Kṣemendra's *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155) [DharmaNexus].
